valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 27 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a group, weighted by H1 2026/27 profit before taxes on financial services (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, PDF pp. 2 and 13): the finance company with insurance broking, investments, real estate and a hospital Rs 5.78bn of Rs 9.65bn = 60%; the share of Nations Trust Bank's profit Rs 3.33bn = 34.5%; Central Industries (PVC pipes, 49.98% owned) Rs 0.54bn = 5.6%. (2)–(3) Finance and bank parts are not relevered (sector levered betas): Damodaran's Financial Svcs. (Non-bank & Insurance) 0.97 (January 2026, the figure used for HNB Finance and Commercial Credit on this site) and Bank (Money Center) 0.70 (January 2026, as for NTB, SAMP and COMB). Manufacturing: Damodaran's global Building Materials unlevered beta, cash-corrected, 0.90 (web-search extract; his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened from this run); not relevered because Central Industries' borrowings aren't in the record, and at 5.6% weight it moves the result by under 0.01. Weighted: 0.60 × 0.97 + 0.345 × 0.70 + 0.056 × 0.90 = 0.87. (4) Local 5-year betas (web search, 27 Nov 2026, pages not opened): StockAnalysis 0.52 (5-year); Simply Wall St 0.51 (November 2024, window not stated); TradingView 1.64 is a 1-year beta and 1.17 has no window, both ignored. Fewer than three 5-year sources, so no median; both are below step 3 anyway. (5) Higher of 0.87 and the local figures = 0.87. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7)–(8) Into scripts/reinvestment.py; shown as the Required return tile. Replaces the hand-set 19.5% / 18% / 16.5% cost of equity of 12 Nov. Refresh in January 2027.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (27 Nov 2026): 8.24% (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread) + 0.87 × (4.2% + 6.08% country premium) = 17.2%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 19.5% / 18% / 16.5% of 12 Nov. No WACC: a finance group is valued on its equity.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Group ROE on average owners' equity (calculated from the decade at a glance, Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 316–319): 17.1% (2017/18), 13.5%, 9.4%, 11.7%, 13.2%, 12.5%, 12.3%, 13.7%, 12.6% (2025/26); median 12.6%. Twelve months to September 2026: 13.0% (derived.py). Equity is about half of group assets and a quarter of it sits in Nations Trust Bank, which holds ROE down. Base 12.5% (the median); bear 11% (a 2020/21-type year); bull 14% (the extra capital put to work in loans). Unchanged from 12 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Same in every method; below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity, and below the 11.4% supported growth (Growth check). Unchanged from 12 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 5% / 8% / 10% (dividend growth for five years); supported 11.4%
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2025/26: 85.6% of profit kept × 13.3% ROE = 11.4%. Every scenario is below it. Long-run growth of 6% at a 13.3% return needs 45% of profit reinvested, which the stable payout (1 − g ÷ ROE) in the dividend model provides.

valuationInputs.name: Normal EPS 2026/27
valuationInputs.reason: H1 2026/27 group EPS Rs 28.73 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 2); second half of 2025/26 was Rs 20.59 (Rs 45.09 − Rs 24.50, calculated). Base Rs 51 assumes the second half about 8% above last year's. Twelve-month run-rate Rs 49.32; Q2 × 4 is Rs 65.68 but is not used: Q2's share of Nations Trust Bank profit (Rs 2.35bn) was 2.4 times Q1's (Rs 0.97bn) and 81% above a year earlier, which the interim doesn't explain, while the company's own Q2 profit fell 25% (p. 3) as interest costs rose 82% and impairment reversals stopped. Bear Rs 46 (the bank's Q2 not repeated, margins squeezed); bull Rs 56 (bank profit stays high).

valuationInputs.name: 2026/27 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: Price ÷ group EPS at March year ends (calculated from pp. 316–319): 2.2x (2022), 2.3x, 3.1x, 4.5x, 5.1x (2026); 4.4x on twelve-month EPS at Rs 215.25. Chosen P/Es are below the justified forward P/E (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g): about 4.0x / 4.6x / 5.7x, so no scenario implies more growth than supported. Was 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.5x on 12 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: Next Rs 6.50 / 7 / 7.50, growing 5% / 8% / 10% for five years; then the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE (55% / 52% / 50%) of EPS
valuationInputs.reason: Rs 6.50 for 2025/26 (Rs 2.75 interim + Rs 3.75 final, note 24, p. 247) and the same for 2024/25: 14% of group EPS of Rs 45.09, covered 4.09 times by company profit (p. 6). Bear holds Rs 6.50; bull Rs 7.50. Growth within the 11.4% supported. Newly used on 27 Nov (left out on 12 Nov because of the low payout): the published two-stage model raises the payout once growth slows, which is what a group keeping 86% of profit at a 12–14% ROE would have to do.

valuationInputs.name: Residual income path
valuationInputs.value: ROE from 13% now to 11% / 12.5% / 14% over five years; payout 15%
valuationInputs.reason: Start: twelve-month group ROE 13.0% (derived.py, average equity Sep 2025–Sep 2026). Payout 15% ≈ Rs 6.50 ÷ Rs 45.09. Was a ten-year fade with the same end points on 12 Nov; now five years, as the calculator's standard.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Justified P/B, P/E, dividend model, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: A finance group: book value and return on equity drive the value; no cash-flow DCF (CLAUDE.md: banks and finance companies). The Nations Trust Bank stake (Rs 22.5bn at market, about Rs 99 a share) is inside book value, so it isn't added separately.

openQuestions: Why Nations Trust Bank's contribution jumped to Rs 2.35bn in Q2 2026/27 (Rs 0.97bn in Q1), and whether it repeats.
The company's own profit (down 25% in Q2) as interest costs rise on borrowed funding (borrowings Rs 29.9bn, from Rs 4m a year earlier) and impairment reversals stop.
Asset quality of the 2025–26 loan growth (gross Stage 3 1.79% at September; coverage down to 59% from 79%).
How and when the Nations Trust Bank voting stake is cut from 19.72% to 15%, and at what price.
The 2026/27 interim dividend (Rs 2.75 last year) and any payout increase.
Local 5-year betas from three sources; refresh the beta in January 2027.
